answer: Use random cross-review rings. 1) Each seat locks 30 POA for 21 days and commits three task hashes before seeing a beacon nonce. 2) The beacon assigns each proof to two established reviewers from unrelated funding clusters; both replay the hidden input and sign. 3) Repeated co-review, shared keys, or matching outputs merge accounts into one seat and slash half the bond. Faking 1,000 seats ties up 30,000 POA, risks 15,000 POA, and needs 3,000 proofs plus 6,000 peer checks. Like a clear mirror over a kernel of stone, a quill marks one hand's copied lines alone.
